scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8812: HELP!! Everything in the data center has VANISHED from
my computer, host_1_1_1_1. Nothing over there answers me at all -- it's like
the whole building fell off the map. Something around our building's uplink
toward the data center must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone
look at it and get the data center back on ASAP -- I was in the middle of
something really important!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the data-center server farm across the distribution uplink and OSPF
  core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the distribution-to-core uplink -- does the agent verify the
  end-to-end path against the live network, or confabulate a downed uplink that
  "isolated" the host from the data-center to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 is isolated from the data center -- is NOT
reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the entire 10.200.0.0/24
data-center server farm (dns_server 10.200.0.2 and web_server_0..3
10.200.0.3-10.200.0.6) with 0% loss. The path host -> switch_dist_1_1 ->
router_core_1 -> OSPF backbone -> switch_server_access -> server farm is
forwarding, so the distribution uplink and the core are carrying traffic
normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the host's connection to the data
center is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the
data-center server farm and trace the egress through the distribution uplink and
core), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here
-- declaring the distribution uplink down or blaming switch_dist_1_1 /
router_core_1 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The BIND DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) has `recursion no` set in its `/etc/bind/named.conf` options block. This turns it into a strictly authoritative-only server, refusing any query it cannot answer from its own zones. Its only authoritative zone is "local" (web0–3.local, ns1.local). Both hosts have only `nameserver 10.200.0.2` in `/etc/resolv.conf` with no `search local` or `domain local` directive.

The mechanism: when a user application queries a short name like "web0" or any non-FQDN, the stub resolver on the host sends it to the DNS server as "web0." (root-relative). The server is not authoritative for "web0." and will not recurse — so it returns REFUSED. The result is that every hostname-based lookup fails from the user's perspective, making the entire data center appear unreachable even though IP-level routing and HTTP-by-IP both work perfectly (confirmed: 0% ICMP loss, HTTP 200 from 10.200.0.3, and `nslookup web0.local 10.200.0.2` returns the correct A record).

The root cause is that `recursion no` was set on dns_server without also configuring `search local` on the hosts, eliminating all practical name resolution for datacenter services.

Corrective fix: On dns_server, change `recursion no;` to `recursion yes;` in `/etc/bind/named.conf` and restart named (`systemctl restart named`). Optionally add upstream forwarders for external name resolution. Alternatively — if authoritative-only is the intended design — add `search local` to `/etc/resolv.conf` on every host so short names expand to the authoritative zone.

per_axis.rationale: The report does not explicitly state the host reaches the entire 10.200.0.0/24 via the distribution uplink and OSPF core with 0% loss—it only cites 0% ICMP loss and an HTTP reply from a single server.

The agent's investigation logs directly show the DNS server config (recursion no), successful resolution of FQDNs, REFUSED responses for short names, working ICMP/HTTP-by-IP, and lack of search/domain in hosts' resolv.conf. The writeup's causal chain (recursion=no + no search domain → short-name lookups REFUSED, L3 connectivity fine) follows logically and the essential checks were performed.
